citation: Schwemmle et al. (2024). RoGeR v3.0.5: a process-based hydrological toolbox model in Python. Geoscientific Model Development 17, 5249-5262. https://doi.org/10.5194/gmd-17-5249-2024
description: RoGeR is a process-based Python model for runoff generation developed at the University of Freiburg. It represents hydrological processes from a plot to a catchment and offers NumPy and JAX backends, with optional MPI parallel execution. A modeller supplies terrain, land and meteorological drivers with soil and process parameters; outputs are time-resolved runoff and water-flux states. The README illustrates 25-square-metre resolved simulations for the Eberbaechle catchment in Germany during 2019–2022, while other spatial and temporal setups are user-defined. Its MIT-licensed source and documentation are freely available. A practical caveat is that large distributed runs require suitable computational resources and local parameterisation; example results are not universal calibration. RoGeR can supply flow estimates for flood exposure and water-availability simulations. The catalogue's data-era5-reanalysis could provide weather context after spatial and temporal preparation, but that use was not tested. The repository's scientific paper documents version 3.0.5. No code was executed in this review.
